svg.title: Level-Funding Economics in Practitioner Numbers
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-level-funding-economics-bars; chapter number: 2; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Level-Funding Economics in Practitioner Numbers; subtitle: Refunds, attachment, savings, and market share reported by operators; unit: percent; caption: Level-funding operators report refunds of unused claim dollars, a 125% aggregate attachment, premium savings of 45% to 60% plus, and mid-market share climbing to 45% of lives.; assumptions note: Where a single figure was reported, min, max, and typical are set equal. The SHP typical refund is the stated current 66% inside the stated 60% to 100% market range.; note: Sources are Security Health Plan, BeneSmart (Rich), Warp, and Dr. Eric Bricker of AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained.; bars: label: SHP Refund on Unused Claim Dollars; min: 60; max: 100; typical: 66; display: 66% now, inside a 60% to 100% market range; label: SHP Aggregate Attachment; min: 125; max: 125; typical: 125; display: 125% aggregate with $10,000 to $20,000 specific; label: Fully Insured to Level-Funded Savings; min: 45; max: 45; typical: 45; display: 45% annual premium savings (BeneSmart); label: Warp Quoted Savings; min: 60; max: 60; typical: 60; display: 60% plus on produced quotes; label: Level-Funded Share in 50-500 Groups; min: 10; max: 45; typical: 45; display: About 10% ten years ago to 45% today

text.title: SHP Refund on Unused Claim Dollars
Assumptions: Where a single figure was reported, min, max, and typical are set equal. The SHP typical refund is the stated current 66% inside the stated 60% to 100% market range.
